tb21_profile.skill: Recover a probabilistic model's dependency structure from observational data (which variables are parents of which, under a stated edge budget and an orientation tie-break rule), fit the conditional parameters, surgically modify the fitted model (do-intervention: cut Y's incoming edges and pin it to a point mass), and forward-sample from the mutilated model.
tb21_profile.domain: Probabilistic graphical models / causal inference / multivariate Gaussian statistics; bnlearn-in-R or pgmpy-in-Python territory, driven off a 10k-row CSV.
tb21_profile.task_form: data-analysis-plus-implement-from-spec: infer hidden structure from data, then produce three exactly-formatted CSV artifacts (edge lists and a resampled dataset).

Use MCMC to estimate the true underlying covariance matrix of observed particle positions - recovering the joint dependence structure from a data sample.
Compute the sensor correlation matrix and repair a broken posterior-inference library built over a Bayesian network architecture; closest TMax match on subject matter.

Extract MAP weights for a Bayesian linear regression; fitting a conditional Gaussian of one variable on its predictors is exactly one node's CPD in this BN.

notes: Nothing in the 76,786-row pool is a Bayesian-network structure-learning task; a regex for 'Bayesian network|bnlearn|pgmpy|structure learning|graphical model' across all seven corpora returns three hits, one of which is the TB2.1 query itself. So the whole ranking is an assembly of the task's parts: dependence estimation from data, conditional-parameter fitting, model surgery, forward sampling. CalibForge wins decisively - five of the final ten - because it is the only corpus with real latent-variable model fitting (HMM, GMM/EM, state-space MLE) and with the fit-structure-then-sample task at rank 1. SWE-Rebench's sdv-dev__rdt entries are the single best find of my own searching: RDT is the Synthetic Data Vault's transform layer, and rdt-832 is precisely 'set a fitted model's parameters by hand, then generate' - retrieval had it buried in rest_ids. Terminal-Lego contributes one genuinely useful item (multiple linear regression from tabular data); the rest of its shortlist is pandas-idiom boilerplate and was the worst false-positive cluster in this packet. Recursive-Task-Synthesis again has NO defensible candidate - its ten are ROOT/CSV extraction chores scoring 1-2, and searches for graph, statistic, pandas and dataframe turned up only infrastructure tasks. TerminalWorld is also thin and its shortlist is unusually FREE-heavy, so eight of my ten came from rest_ids or search. Downstream: if only one corpus can be sampled for this TB2.1 task, take CalibForge.
